Not sure if there has been any movement on this that hasn't been tracked on here specifically, but I would argue for 

> Is disabled restorable state

that for the custom element reaction, that specific state should be opt-in-able via the state previously set on `ElementInternals.prototype.setFormValue` since that method accepts both a form value and a state. Although it appears as if even [Chrome is no longer calling `formStateRestoreCallback` with the previous state, only the value](https://codepen.io/calebdwilliams/pen/eYVPZBW?editors=1010)(warning: overly-simplistic demo).

What I'm confused about (and maybe this is a separate issue) is how, exactly, the `formStateRestore` reaction should be triggered in the case of autocomplete. This is beginning to be an issue for the teams I support. If this is the right place to discuss that behavior, let me know; otherwise, I'd be happy to create a new issue.

Hi,

I noticed that this issue might be causing problems like hydration mismatches when using a framework like Nuxt JS and UI components libraries (e.g., Nuxt UI). For example, setting a loading state on a button or another form component would also apply `disabled = true,` causing a hydration mismatch when reloading the page.

I put together a [StackBlitz](https://stackblitz.com/edit/nuxt-starter-3c8vwwjq) test in which I made two custom components (CustomButton and CustomButtonWithoutDisabled). The first one will put the button in a loading and disabled state when its property loading is set to `true`. The second one will just put it in a loading state—add a spinner and some styling. Upon reloading the page, the CustomButton component will have a hydration mismatch, while the CustomButtonWithoutDisabled component has no issue.

My opinion on the matter is that caching the disabled state should be in line with what other browsers are doing. If not, it causes unexpected behaviour only in Firefox, and developers need to create workarounds for one browser. Also, those workarounds might not always be straightforward when using libraries.

I also opened a related issue on the Nuxt framework repo before realizing this might be a browser problem.

Nuxt JS issue: [Hydration issue in Firefox #31296](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/31296)
StackBlitz example: [StackBlitz](https://stackblitz.com/edit/nuxt-starter-3c8vwwjq)
